sections.name: ErrorBoundaryProps
sections.title: Settings for the safety wrapper
sections.what: Lists the children, reset keys, region label and test id.
sections.why: Lets callers name the region and choose when it should retry.
sections.watch_out: Arrays or objects built fresh on every render always count as changed, which can keep the wrapper retrying.

sections.name: ErrorBoundaryState
sections.title: What is remembered about an error
sections.what: Holds the error and its component stack, or nothing when the section is healthy.
sections.why: Needed to decide whether to show the fallback.

sections.name: resetKeysChanged
sections.title: Checking whether reset keys changed
sections.what: Compares old and new reset keys one by one, and reports a change if the count or any value differs.
sections.why: Likely reason: automatic recovery should only happen when the inputs really changed.
sections.watch_out: Comparison is strict, so new but equal-looking objects count as changed.

sections.name: ErrorBoundary (part 1)
sections.title: Catching and logging errors
sections.what: Stores the error when a child crashes, logs it with the component stack, clears the error when keys change, and builds the text of the details.
sections.why: Keeps the full error available for copying into a bug report, as the code comment says.
sections.watch_out: The log only appears in the browser console, which users do not normally open.

sections.name: ErrorBoundary (part 2)
sections.title: Fallback panel
sections.what: Shows the region name with the failed to render text, a Retry button, a note that the rest of the page still works, and the error details in a scrolling box.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user report the error without facing a blank page.
sections.watch_out: The details box shows raw stack text, which is meant for reporting rather than for ordinary users.

summary: A safety wrapper that catches a crash inside one part of the page and shows the error with details instead of a blank screen.
purpose: Keeps one broken section from taking down the whole app.
why: The code comment says it is an extra safety net that keeps the error visible and logged rather than swallowed.
how: Wraps its children. If one of them throws, it stores the error and stack, logs it to the console, and shows a fallback panel with a Retry button. The error clears when the reset keys change or Retry is pressed.
inputs: Child content, optional reset keys, a region label and a test id.
outputs: Either the normal content or a fallback panel, plus a console log entry.
risks: The fallback shows the full error and stack text, which can reveal internal details. Errors raised in event handlers are not caught by this wrapper.
debug: Read the console message beginning with ErrorBoundary. Check the region name in the fallback heading. If it keeps failing, check whether the reset keys change too often.
